items.claim: The single-proverb call for 10:9 is well warranted: 10:8 and 10:10 share a byte-identical closing colon that brackets v.9 on both sides, and the drafted treatment of both flanking verses independently confirms the same envelope without absorbing v.9 into it.
items.evidence: oshb byte comparison shows Prov.10.8 and Prov.10.10 close with the identical colon וֶאֱוִ֥יל שְׂ֝פָתַ֗יִם יִלָּבֵֽט (verse_map_oshb.json); 10:9's own path-integrity pair shares no word-level token with that refrain; the corpus draft for both Prov.10.8 and Prov.10.10 independently names the same shared B-line and rejects folding v.9 into either, corroborating this boundary from both sides.

items.claim: The 10:16-17 cluster's rare-phrase cohesion re-verifies cleanly, but device_notes mischaracterizes both cola as lacking an adversative when 10:17's own WEB rendering contains an explicit "but," contradicting the row's stated criterion and this writer's own consistent practice of labeling every other but-bearing bicolon in the surrounding verses as antithetic.
items.evidence: Independent skeleton sweep of לחיים over all 915 oshb verses returns exactly 4 hits (Prov.10.16, Prov.10.17, Prov.11.19, Prov.19.23), Prov.10.16-Prov.10.17 the only adjacent pair, matching the row's claim; word-level adjacent-token check across Prov.10.6-10.29 finds no other undisclosed distinctive token at either cluster boundary (10:15|10:16, 10:17|10:18 both clean). But web:Prov.10.17 itself reads “He is in the way of life who heeds correction, but he who forsakes reproof leads others astray.” -- containing "but" -- directly contradicting the device_notes claim that both cola lack an adversative; every other bicolon in Prov.10.6-29 whose WEB text contains "but" is labeled antithetic in its own device_notes (10:9, 10:18, 10:21, 10:24, 10:25, 10:27), so this reads as an isolated, checkable inconsistency rather than a considered classification choice.

items.claim: 10:18's boundaries are clean at word level against both neighbors; the only apparent overlap with 10:19 is a substring artifact rather than a shared word-level token, and the underlying root is too diffuse across this chapter to count as local seam evidence.
items.evidence: Word-level skeleton token check finds no shared content token between Prov.10.17|10.18 or Prov.10.18|10.19; the construct form in 10:18 and the suffixed form in 10:19 differ as whole-word tokens despite one being a substring of the other; that root recurs at Prov.10.8, 10.10, 10.13, 10.18, 10.19, 10.21 -- six of about twenty-four verses in this stretch -- consistent with the toolkit's own caution against treating diffuse chapter vocabulary as a boundary device.

items.claim: 10:20's metals-valuation imagery is unique to this verse in its stretch; the only tokens it shares with either neighbor are book-wide-common, far too frequent to serve as catchword-grade cohesion under the same rarity bar the writer applied to the adjacent 10:16-17 cluster claim.
items.evidence: Word-level check: Prov.10.19|10.20 shares no content token; Prov.10.20|10.21 shares only צדיק (34/915), לב (47/915), both independently swept over all 915 oshb verses.

items.claim: 10:21's feeding/starvation bicolon is correctly kept atomic; its shared tokens with 10:20 are book-wide-common rather than catchword-grade, that boundary is independently closed from the 10:20 side as well, so arguing the 10:22 boundary instead is a defensible pick of the more topically proximate rival, not a strawman.
items.evidence: Word-level check confirms Prov.10.20|10.21 shares only common tokens (צדיק (34/915), לב (47/915)); Prov.10.21|10.22 shares no content token at all; the corpus draft for Prov.10.20 independently states no pairing is drawn with either neighbor, closing the loop on the boundary this row does not restate.

items.claim: 10:24's fear/desire bicolon shares no content token at all with 10:23 and only a book-wide-common token with 10:25, so the atomic call is clean and the chosen rival (10:25's judgment-adjacent storm image) is a fairer pick than the lexically and thematically disconnected 10:23.
items.evidence: Word-level check: Prov.10.23|10.24 shares zero content tokens; Prov.10.24|10.25 shares only רשע (36/915), independently swept.

items.claim: 10:25's storm/foundation bicolon is correctly held apart from 10:26's construction-marked tricolon simile, and the 10:24/10:25 boundary this row does not restate is independently closed from the 10:24 side, so coverage across the pair is complete.
items.evidence: The corpus draft for Prov.10.26 independently names its simile construction as the reason it stands apart from both 10:25 and 10:27; word-level check finds only the common token רשע (36/915) at the 10:24|10:25 boundary, already dismissed in the 10:24 draft.

items.claim: 10:27's fear-of-Yahweh lifespan bicolon is correctly atomized; it shares only a book-wide-common token with 10:28, its YHWH token is properly held in device_notes as texture rather than promoted to a boundary driver, and the 10:26/10:27 boundary this row does not restate is independently closed from the 10:26 side.
items.evidence: Word-level check: Prov.10.27|10.28 shares only רשעים (35/915), independently swept; prov_device_inventory.json's yhwh_density lists chapter 10 at 4 occurrences total, consistent with texture-only framing rather than an isolated driver claim.
